subject: MSA Exhibit B — billing lanes, commits, and tax residency confirmation
messages:
From: Emma Rutledge <emma.rutledge@acmecorp.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Exhibit B (billing lanes & withholding)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. Procurement asked me to circle back on two items in the MSA Exhibit B: the billing lanes for mixed-region usage, and how Redwood wants to handle withholding / VAT evidence for EU-covered spends. Specific asks: 

- Can you confirm whether we will receive one consolidated invoice per month or per-entity split invoices if usage crosses subsidiaries?
- We need clarity on net terms: legal prefers Net 60 for new suppliers; is Redwood able to accommodate Net 60 on this agreement?
- On taxes: Acme needs a clear path for providing reverse-charge evidence or W-8/W-9 equivalents — we cannot accept a blanket clause that places withholding risk solely with our procurement team.

Please see attached procurement packet (Procurement checklist + entity matrix). If you can flag which parts of Exhibit B we should prioritize, that will help speed legal/finance review.

Attachments: Acme_Procurement_Packet.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Emma Rutledge
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Rutledge <emma.rutledge@acmecorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B (billing lanes & withholding)

Emma — thanks, appreciate the clear list. Looping Ben here for payment ops details; Ben — quick read attached (ExhibitB_Draft_2026.pdf) with the current language from legal. High level responses inline below and a suggested path to close: 

1) Invoice cadence / entity split: Redwood can provide either a consolidated invoice or per-entity invoices depending on Acme's preferred remit mapping. If you need per-entity invoices we will require the remit mapping matrix (name, tax id, remit email) and this will be reflected as separate invoice recipients. Operationally, per-entity splits may push additional PO mapping work but are supported.

2) Net terms: We typically ship Net 30 or Net 45 on hosted customers by default. For enterprise commitments and specific procurement constraints, we can consider Net 60 but it will need a commercial anchor (either a modest increase to the invoice schedule or an onboarding activation fee to offset extended DSO). Ben — can you confirm the commercial trade-off we can offer for Net 60?

3) Withholding / tax evidence: We accept reverse-charge documentation for EU transactions (local VAT reg numbers, electronic confirmation) and can support recipient-side documentation rather than assuming withholding. For US customers requiring W-9/W-8 forms, our tax team will accept the standard forms; any gross-up requests will need to be captured in Exhibit B as a clause.

Next steps I propose: 
- Ben to propose a Net 60 commercial offset and confirm how that shows in Exhibit B.
- I’ll send a redline of Exhibit B that marks invoice cadence, activation fee language, and a clause for evidence submission for reverse-charge.
- If Acme can share a remit matrix we’ll draft a sample per-entity invoice for review.

Attachment: ExhibitB_Draft_2026.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-31T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA Exhibit B — suggested redlines for Net 60 / invoicing lanes

Team — forwarding Marcus’s exchange with Acme. I attached my redline and a short commercial note: ExhibitB_Marcus_Redline.docx (redlines). TL;DR suggested approach: 

- Net terms: Allow Net 60 as an exception with a 1.5% surcharge applied to invoices older than 45 days (simple commercial offset) OR apply a one-time onboarding activation fee equal to 1% of first-quarter committed spend. Prefer the activation fee option for strategic deals.

- Minimum commit: Confirmed $250k annual minimum across consolidated account; if Acme requests per-entity split, require a pro-rated min-commit per entity with a 30-day PO window.

- Invoicing lanes / remit: Support per-entity invoice delivery if Acme provides a remit matrix. Add a short paragraph to Exhibit B that Redwood will not be liable for delayed payment caused by mismatched remit information supplied by customer.

- Tax / withholding: Add a process paragraph: customer provides tax evidence (VAT reg numbers, tax residency certificate) within 30 days of first invoice; Redwood will apply reverse-charge treatment on subsequent invoices if evidence is validated. If evidence isn’t provided, taxes are assessed per legal language and customer remains responsible.

I flagged the exact clause locations in the docx. Can legal (Kimberly) confirm redline legality and any regulatory risk? Lauren — can you confirm the accounting treatment for the proposed activation fee vs surcharge?

Attachments: ExhibitB_Marcus_Redline.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Ben / team — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed Ben’s options with Acme finance: 

- Acme can accept Net 60 for the initial 12-month term if Redwood accepts the onboarding activation fee (1% of Q1 committed spend) in lieu of the surcharge. Finance will route the activation fee to a separate PO.
- We will provide the remit mapping matrix by EOD Thursday; please confirm the expected format (csv or template).
- On withholding: Acme will provide VAT registration numbers for EU entities and a signed tax residency letter. We expect Redwood to apply reverse-charge from the second invoice month after validation.

If that aligns, we can get legal to sign the limited Exhibit B amendment and push to DocuSign. Please send the redline that incorporates the activation fee language and the 30-day evidence window. Also include a DocuSign link when the final is ready.
